name: CIV
label: Revelation
lede: Three-quarters of Gorilla Biscuits, a songwriter who wasn't in the band, a homemade video that made it to Buzz Bin, and a debut that took a New York hardcore band into MTV's Buzz Bin.

eras.title: Gorilla Biscuits under another name
eras.text: Gorilla Biscuits had broken up, and Walter Schreifels was busy making heavy records with Quicksand. He still had fast, funny, hooky songs in him, and he knew exactly which friends should play them. The band got named after its singer.

years.cap: Civ, Charlie Garriga, Arthur Smilios, Sammy Siegler
years.p: Singer [[Anthony Civarelli|a5d69704-924b-4128-9577-e16531503890]] and bassist [[Arthur Smilios|40d4f905-3bb1-4d2e-9a9b-1d7891033094]] come from Gorilla Biscuits; drummer [[Sammy Siegler|869c662b-574c-46ac-acf6-3dc6f025fd5a]] has already done [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]] and [[Judge|3827fbb6-e219-4e2d-9af8-35cc9a7d8d8e]]. [[Charlie Garriga|4f24f7e7-bc37-45d1-8f60-99bc992cd780]] plays guitar. The band is CIV, after the singer.
years.xp:
Smilios had finished school and missed playing. Schreifels, now in a band that had signed to a major, reunited a late version of his old group around songs he'd written.

Why not just call it Gorilla Biscuits? Schreifels said he wanted freedom to try new things and be funnier, without hardcore's owners' manual hanging over it.

years.h: The songwriter who isn't in the band
years.p: Schreifels writes the bulk of the debut and co-produces it with [[Don Fury|0bec484f-b890-4823-af64-0e48530f6f6f]]. Recording runs from 1994 into 1995. It's a break from Quicksand's weight: hardcore songs that aren't heavy.

eras.title: Buzz Bin
eras.text: A hardcore band from the Revelation family landed on a major-label imprint, made a video for almost nothing, and ended up on MTV and on Beavis and Butt-head. It was about as far into the mainstream as a band out of the NYHC matinees had gone.

years.p: The Atlantic imprint run by Jason Flom takes the band. Smilios said later he would have stayed independent.
Produced by Don Fury and Schreifels, mixed by Michael Barbiero. The singles also come out on Revelation vinyl. Years later a Bay Area band will name itself Set Your Goals after it.

years.cap: The talk-show video, directed by Marcos Siega
q: We made the video ourselves and it got on MTV.
years.h: A perfectly crappy video on MTV
years.p: Can't Wait One Minute More, with [[Lou Koller|f1549cac-a48c-4741-8edd-09c1016ada64]] of [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]] on guest vocals, gets a talk-show-parody video directed by Marcos Siega. It goes into MTV's Buzz Bin, onto Beavis and Butt-head, and to No. 21 on Billboard's Modern Rock Tracks.
years.xp:
Schreifels called it the best pairing of song and video he ever had, and he meant the cheapness as praise. Choices Made got a video too.

The song kept turning up for a decade: a Nissan commercial around 2005, What's New, Scooby-Doo?, Mega Man and Road Rash 3D.

years.p: CIV lands on the soundtrack to Escape from L.A.. More singles follow on Lava and Atlantic.

eras.title: The getaway
eras.text: The second record came without Schreifels as the main writer, with a new crop of producers and a scene in mourning. It split critics hard, and within two years the band called a halt.

years.p: Arthur leaves before the second album is finished; [[Cache Tolman|1d48168d-10f9-48f7-9cb9-622f1a0e39c1]] comes in on bass. Schreifels contributes a single song this time.

q: It was a great record that was about a decade ahead of its time.
years.p: Produced by Michael Barbiero, John Goodmanson and Steve Thompson, and dedicated to Raybeez of [[Warzone|496da466-68e9-4cbb-9e86-cbb57eda861a]]. Reviews run from a 1.0 at Pitchfork to a 7.5 at Germany's Rock Hard.
years.xp:
The Plain Dealer heard one more post-[[Green Day|084308bd-1654-436f-ba03-df6697104e19]] band. The San Diego Union-Tribune heard pop hooks with a punk charge. Nobody heard the same record.

Smilios, who'd left before it was done, has defended it ever since.

years.p: The album's single, released a month after the record.
After two albums, CIV announces a permanent hiatus.

eras.title: Goals, revisited
eras.text: The reunions came as one-offs, each built around an occasion: a hardcore bowling-alley weekend, a Belgian festival, a New York ballroom. Nobody announced a new album.

years.h: Back at the Black N Blue Bowl
years.p: The first CIV show since the hiatus.
The European festival puts CIV back on a big stage.
A New York headline night on 11th Street.

eras.title: Sharing a bill with Shelter
eras.text: Siegler had been back in Shelter since 2018. In 2024 the two bands went out together.

years.h: On tour with Shelter, then the Netherlands
years.p: CIV plays a run with [[Shelter|d5157104-76b1-4b8b-90c2-9ff994f940db]] and a show in the Netherlands.
